summary: Tested StumbleChat v2 architectural overhaul (Google+Guest auth, tabbed SPA, persistent chats, blocks, hotlist, stumble_id, telegram_id). 17/17 backend pytest cases pass after fixing one CRITICAL backend bug (falsy-projection bug returning 404 'User not found' on /api/conversations/{peer}/messages). Frontend E2E confirms auth UX, guest gating, tabbed SPA, people search, chats empty state, settings page work. One gap remains: _upsert_email_user does NOT auto-generate stumble_id for first-time OTP users (and does not init hotlist/blocked/telegram_id), so Profile/Settings stumble-id-display is hidden for email-OTP users.

critical.endpoint: POST /api/conversations/{peer_user_id}/messages (and any handler using same projection pattern)
critical.issue: Used `if not peer_doc:` after a Mongo projection `{'_id':0,'blocked':1,'hotlist':1}`. For older users without those fields, the projection returns `{}` (falsy dict) but the user actually exists → handler returns 404 'User not found' for ALL existing email-OTP users. FIXED by changing to `if peer_doc is None:`. Recommend auditing other handlers (delete_message, hotlist, block) for same pattern.

minor.issue: Does not auto-generate `stumble_id`, nor initialize `hotlist`/`blocked`/`telegram_id`/`gender`/`interested_in`/`bio`/`images` fields. Spec says 'New user (Google or first OTP) gets a unique @stumble_id auto-generated'. Should call _generate_unique_stumble_id(name) and seed empty arrays/strings on insert. Currently email users get blank stumble_id forever which also hides the Stumble ID display on Profile and Settings.

ui_bugs.issue: stumble-id-display and settings-stumble-id are conditionally rendered on `profile.stumble_id` being truthy. Because backend never sets stumble_id for email-OTP users, these elements are never visible. Will resolve when backend gap above is fixed.

integration_issues.issue: wss://.../api/socket.io upgrades fail with 403 in the preview ingress (only polling works). Socket.IO does fall back to polling and connect event still fires, so Live badge should still flip — but persistent socket-based realtime (direct_message, message_deleted) will rely on polling latency. Not in this turn's scope to fix, but worth noting.

action_items: Update _upsert_email_user in /app/backend/server.py to auto-generate stumble_id (call _generate_unique_stumble_id) AND initialize hotlist=[], blocked=[], telegram_id='', gender='', interested_in='', interests=[], bio='', images=[] on insert. Without this, Profile/Settings hide the Stumble ID block and search/share-by-handle is impossible for email users.

Audit all other handlers that use the projection pattern `{'_id':0,'blocked':1,'hotlist':1}` (or similar partial projections) and switch `if not doc:` → `if doc is None:`. Suspect locations: send_message (fixed), delete_message, hotlist toggle, block toggle, send-photo, conversation delete.
Consider a one-time backfill migration: for users where stumble_id is missing/empty, generate one via _generate_unique_stumble_id(name).
(Optional) WSS 403 from ingress — main agent may want to verify socket.io transports=['polling','websocket'] order or document polling-only for preview env.
critical_code_review_comments: Bug: `if not peer_doc:` is unsafe when the same query uses projections that may yield {} for older docs. Use explicit `is None` checks everywhere.

DRY: _upsert_email_user and _upsert_user_from_google have diverged in fields set on insert — extract a shared `_default_user_fields(provider)` helper to ensure parity (stumble_id, blocked, hotlist, telegram_id) across auth providers.
server.py is now 1838+ lines — recommend splitting routers (auth, profile, conversations, block/hotlist, admin) into separate modules.

Conditional UI rendering on backend-provided fields (e.g., `{profile.stumble_id && ...}`) silently hides important features when backend omits the field. Either default to a placeholder + 'Generating…' or always render and gray-out.

rca of the issue: RCA — 404 'User not found' on every message send: Repro: any email-OTP user (created via /api/auth/email/verify-otp) POSTs to /api/conversations/{any_existing_peer}/messages. Result: 404. Root cause: handler queried `users_collection.find_one({'user_id': peer_user_id}, {'_id':0,'blocked':1,'hotlist':1})`. For older users created by `_upsert_email_user` (which never set `blocked`/`hotlist`), Mongo returns an empty dict `{}` (the doc exists but projection has no requested fields). The handler then `if not peer_doc:` evaluated to True (empty dict is falsy) and returned 404. Mitigation applied: `if peer_doc is None:`. Long-term mitigation: also fix _upsert_email_user to seed default arrays/fields so all users have a consistent shape — see action items.
